candidateDecisions.label: Mechanical engineering, sensors & sustainable manufacturing
candidateDecisions.assessment: Robotics contributes kinematics and practical automation, and Consumer Product Design covers design, prototyping and repairability. These do not supply the mechanics, electronic instrumentation, materials processing and fabrication progression needed for a separate engineering-focused option.

analysis: The closest plan directly pursues circular product development and material recovery. Consumer Product Design develops needs assessment, specifications, prototypes and scaling with explicit repairability and lifespan, followed by Life Cycle Analysis and Circular Economy. Recycling, Recovery, Remediation includes laboratory separation, leaching and analytical work on solar-panel and waste recovery. Environmental Biogeochemistry adds chemical modelling and laboratory interpretation, Renewable System Design adds technical and economic evaluation of energy use, and Robotics applies kinematics and motion planning with a programmable arm. These implement the target's design, modelling and circular resource aims without providing its chemical-engineering progression. The life science plan applies cell biology and biochemistry to sustainable production questions, with laboratory culture, transformation, protein purification and DNA analysis, sustainable agriculture, biodiversity, resource recovery, nature-based design and life-cycle assessment. It addresses the biological and production theme while lacking industrial fermentation, bioreactor design and separation engineering. A manufacturing-focused palette was tested against robotics, linear systems, product design, maths, programming, environmental materials and reuse. Its control, sensing and prototyping applications are relevant, but the workbook does not sustain mechanical physics, electronic instrumentation, fabrication or materials production as a separate organising pathway. Thus the two options pass the programme-level comparability and distinctness checks as qualified comparisons. Research in a Sustainable Delta is offered only before the intended foundations. The revised placements use design, robotics and life-cycle assessment, with Earth System Science Tools moved to an available spring. The comparative plan offers no claim of equivalence or professional progression.
